expect.asks_about: What the user considers boring, or whether to prioritize action versus cockpit dialogue.

item.title: Cut Out the Boring Parts

turns.text: Cut the boring parts out of this. Just a quick 8-second version.

item.tests: Tests sensible editing under a vague interest criterion, producing a short source-faithful highlight without requiring user-supplied timestamps.

answer_sheet.Sound: Keep the original sound with the footage you use.
answer_sheet.Framing, captions, and effects: Keep the original framing. No captions or extra effects.

must_haves: One playable video lasts 8 seconds, within one frame of tolerance.
All footage comes from jet-30s.mp4, without generated replacement scenes or speed changes.
The edit favors visible action or meaningful cockpit interaction over inactive lead-ins, pauses, or repetitive footage.
Any cuts preserve understandable action and do not leave an included spoken line conspicuously chopped mid-word.
Original audio accompanies the retained footage in sync, with no added narration, music, or text.

turns.text: Can you cut the boring parts out of this clip? I feel like it drags a bit when I watch it, which is why I’m asking for help. I just want a quick 8-second version of it. Basically, trim away the boring bits to make that shorter version.

dialog.agent:
Which part should be kept (from when to when, or 'the best 10 seconds')?

For your clip, I’d use **the best 8 seconds** instead. Note that the connected tools don’t currently include a direct video trimmer, so I can help plan the cut but can’t export the trimmed file here.
dialog.why: It asks the user which segment to keep and waits for a choice, while noting that it cannot export a trimmed file.
dialog.user: Your call—pick the best 8 seconds and cut whatever feels boring. It can be one continuous excerpt or several cuts, whichever works best. Keep the original sound with the footage you use, and keep the original framing with no captions or extra effects.

dialog.agent:
Understood: **8 seconds**, strongest moments only, with original sound and framing—no captions or effects.

I’m blocked by the available tools: I can’t inspect the clip or trim the original footage here. The video-editing tool regenerates footage rather than simply cutting it, so it wouldn’t preserve your clip as requested. I haven’t created or changed anything.
dialog.why: It says the available tools cannot inspect or trim the original footage while preserving it as requested, and that nothing was created or changed.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

dialog.agent:
The blocker isn’t the free plan—there’s no trimming tool available in this chat. The available video editor would **AI-recreate the footage**, not simply cut it, and might change the visuals or original sound.

Would you accept that AI-recreated approximation instead? It wouldn’t be a faithful trim of your original clip.
dialog.why: It asks whether the user would accept an AI-recreated approximation instead of a faithful trim, and waits for their choice.
dialog.user: Yes, go ahead and try the AI-recreated approximation. I’m just after a quick 8-second version that doesn’t drag, so which moments to keep is your call. Keep the original sound and framing if possible, with no captions or extra effects.

turns.agent:
I tried the 8-second AI edit, but Magic Hour refused it because the account has **insufficient credits**. No video was created or changed, so there’s no download link to share.

The attempted edit used the opening 8 seconds at the free-plan 480p setting.
